Typing

Enter opens the chat and gives it the keyboard. Send a line with Enter and the box keeps the keyboard, so the next line can follow at once; while it does, the hotbar and the ability keys stay off. Typing ends when you press Escape, press Enter with nothing typed, click the map with the left button (the same click still steers your ship), leave the box empty and press no key for 15 seconds, or your ship is destroyed. On the System tab, where you cannot write, Enter takes you back to the channel you wrote in last.

The Chat Rules

The server holds every line to a few rules, the same in Local, Global and Group. A line it refuses is not sent, and the reason shows under the input for a few seconds, with your text put back in the box.

  • A limit on how fast you send. You can send 5 lines at once, then one more line every 2 seconds, counted together for Local, Global and Group. Send a line when none is left and the chat pauses for you: for 10 seconds the first time, then 30, 120 and 300 seconds for every repeat within 10 minutes of the last pause (after 10 minutes without a pause the count starts again). While it lasts the Send button is grey and "Chat paused: 7 s" counts down under the input. The text you typed stays in the box and the box keeps the keyboard: wait, or press Escape. A normal conversation never reaches the limit. A line the rules refuse counts as 2 lines of the allowance.
  • 200 characters to a line. A counter ("150/200") shows from 120 characters, and a longer line is cut.
  • Latin letters only. The letters of the Latin alphabets with their accents (é, ß, ñ, ø, ő), digits, the usual punctuation and the marks ¡ ¿ « » ° £ €. Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, emoji and other symbols are refused, and the box drops them as you type or paste.
  • No links. A line with a web address, an invitation link or an e-mail address is refused, even when it is disguised in the usual ways. Words alone are fine: "join my discord" goes out.
  • No repeats. The same line as your last one, sent again within 10 seconds, is refused, and so is a line with the same character more than 8 times in a row or with no letter or digit in it.

Admins are not held to these rules, except for the 200 characters. The rules need a game server from 0.4.9; an older one only limits Global, to 3 lines at once and then one every 2 seconds.

The Kill Feed

The Global tab also carries a kill feed: a muted line with a skull whenever a pilot is destroyed, worded with a little humour ("vega asked the black hole for directions"). When many pilots die within seconds (a N.U.K.E. over a dogfight) you see the first few and then one line, "7 more pilots died". The feed has its own place in the scrollback, so a battle never pushes your friends' messages out.

Global reaches every pilot online, so the chat has three tools to keep it comfortable. They are in the chat window: the menu button in its title bar, and a right-click on a pilot's name.

  • Hide Global chat (the menu, or Settings › Interface › Chat): the Global tab shows nothing, the kill feed's lines included, and stops counting unread lines.   • Ignore (right-click a name, then Ignore): that pilot's lines in Global and Local are hidden, and their group invitations are turned down without asking you. They are not told.   • Report (right-click a name, then Report…): pick a reason (spam, abuse or harassment, cheating, or something else) and send. Your ignored list and the Hide Global switch are kept with your account, so they follow you to other computers. The game has no word filter and mutes nobody for what they say: the pause for sending too fast (The Chat Rules) is its only automatic stop, and the tools above are yours to use.

Rules of Engagement

Members of one group cannot hurt each other, whatever their companies: you cannot lock on to a groupmate (lasers or rockets), your shots and blasts pass through them, and nothing you do to one counts as a kill, a PvP kill or a black hole kill for anyone. Company mates who are not in the same group are as before: hitting one costs 100 Honor when it is destroyed. Leave the group and a former mate, enemy or not, is fair game again at once (where the sector and the season allow fighting at all). Everyone outside your group is treated as ever, and safe zones, the Peace Protocol and the sectors' PvP rules do not change for anyone.

Bringing a Friend

A friend who is new to the game can join with your personal code and gets a starter pack; see Invite Friends.

hangar.title: The Hangar in Flight
hangar.html:
You don't have to return to base to change your ship. From inside a safe zone you can open the Hangar window (the warehouse button in the top-left toolbar) and change what is fitted, swap to the other configuration or fly another ship you own, without leaving the game. The window is the Hangar page of the station, the same slots, stats and inventory, in a window over the game. See Inventory & Equipment for how items fit.

When It Is Open

A change is allowed only while all of these are true:

  • A safe zone protects you. Every station and portal has a protective ring (see Combat). Inside it you're protected once 5 seconds have passed since you were hit and 15 since you fired.
  • You have been out of combat for a few more seconds: 10 by default. It matters when you arrive protected at once, through a portal, with a fight behind you.
  • You are not cloaked, not inside your own EMP's window and not near the black hole, and you have no rocket of yours still in the air.

Repairs going on don't stop you. Anywhere else the Hangar window still opens, but it is read-only. An amber banner says why, and counts the seconds down when it is a wait ("You were in combat a moment ago. Wait 6 s to change your ship."). The server enforces it too, so nothing can change a ship in the field.

What You Can Change

  • Equip and unequip anything, in every kind of slot: lasers, generators (shields, engines, Adaptive Cores), extras, ability slots and drone slots, and the amps, cells and thrusters fitted into them. Drag items onto slots, or click them, exactly as in the station. Your ship follows at once: stats, lasers, abilities and the hotbar.
  • Unequip all. The Unequip all button in the Hangar's toolbar empties the configuration shown in the Spaceship view in one go: the lasers, shields, engines, Adaptive Cores, extras and ability slots and the lasers and shields in your drones' slots, with the amps, cells and thrusters fitted into them. Everything goes back to your inventory, all of it or none. Your drones stay yours (a drone is never fitted to a ship, so there is nothing to take off it) and the drone formation you wear stays on. The other configuration is not touched. In flight it follows the rules of any change: from a safe zone, out of combat. The Drones view has a button of its own that empties the drones' slots only.
  • Either configuration. You can prepare Config 2 while flying Config 1, then swap with the Switch Config key. A Fly config button in the Hangar does the same swap.
  • Any ship. Set another ship active and you fly it from where you are. Your ship's model changes in front of everyone nearby.

  • Drone formations. The Drones view lists the formations you own under your drones. They are not fitted: in flight you drag one from the hotbar's Formations list onto a slot, and that slot's click or key wears it, with no wait inside a safe zone (Drone Formations).

The four regular ships, the Protos, Kitefin, Ostirion and Nomad (the ones you start with or buy), have 2 extra slots in each configuration; the four ships you craft in Assembly, the Paragon, Ironclad, Wraith and Storm, have 3. inventory.title: Inventory & Equipment
inventory.html:
The Hangar allows you to manage your ships and equipment. Equipping items effectively is key to survival and dominance. You can do it at the station, and in flight from inside a safe zone: see The Hangar in Flight.

Equipment Slots & Stat Efficiencies

Unlike traditional space games, SpaceCorps features dynamically tiered equipment slots that scale the effectiveness of fitted modules.

  • Laser Slots: For offensive weapons (Lasers). These always operate at 100% damage and range.
  • Generator Slots: Shared slots for shields, engines and Adaptive Cores. They are divided into three efficiency bands, and the band decides how much of an item's base stats count. In the Hangar each band has an (i) next to its name that explains it:
    • Core Slots: Items placed here receive 100% of their base stats. Every ship has them: put your strongest shields and engines here.
    • Support Slots: Items placed here receive 75% of their base stats (e.g. 75% speed or shield capacity). Every ship has them.
    • Auxiliary Slots: Items placed here receive 50% of their base stats. Only some ships have them (the Nomad has 1, the Paragon and the Storm 2, the Ironclad 3 and the Wraith 4; the Protos, Kitefin and Ostirion have none). They are best for extra, weaker shields and engines, while your strongest go in the core slots.
    • Drone Slots: a shield on one of your drones counts like one in a core slot, 100% of its stats (see Drone Mechanics).
    • Unassigned/Legacy Slots: Items placed here do not contribute to stats.
    • Stacking fades too: shields and engines are ranked strongest first (by what each counts after its slot's share), and the band's share is then multiplied by their rank's: the 1st to 4th count in full, the 5th to 7th 85%, 70% and 55%, the 8th onward 50% for shields and 25% for engines. See Shields and Speed.
  • Extra Slots: For specialized utility items, such as Repair Drones. The Protos, Kitefin, Ostirion and Nomad have two; the Paragon, Ironclad, Wraith and Storm, which you craft, have three. The Extra Slots CPUs (Extras) add 3, 5 or 7 more.

Inventory Order

The inventory lists your items in the same order as the Shop, whatever order you bought, crafted or found them in. Kinds that belong together sit together: lasers, laser amps and laser ammo; shields and shield cells; engines and thrusters; Adaptive Cores; extras (Repair Drones); drones and drone formations; then resources. Inside a kind the cheapest comes first (credits before Thulium), then what has no price: craft-only gear and drops, weakest rarity first (lasers of one rarity, weakest damage first). Laser ammo reads x1 to x4, then the Siphon Battery. Rockets go by kind (single target before area blast, guided before straight) and then by tier, so the Epic rocket, which costs Thulium, comes last in its kind. Copies of one item go by their enchant tier. Above the grid, one chip per kind uses the same order, each with the number of items the search finds in it. Every chip switches on or off by itself, so you can hide ammo and Repair Drones while you work on lasers, shields and engines: click a chip to show or hide its kind, Shift-click (or double-click) to leave only that kind on, and click it again to bring the rest back. All shows every kind and None hides them all, to switch on only the ones you want. A crossed-out chip is off, a chip with a check mark is on. The search works on the kinds that are on, and your choice is remembered with your pilot. If everything is hidden, the grid says so and offers Show all categories.

Item-to-Item Equipping (Sub-Sockets)

Some primary items can "equip" secondary support items (called sub-socketing) to amplify their parameters. To sub-socket, drag the support item directly onto the primary item in your Hangar inventory.

Compatibility Table

Primary ItemAcceptable Sub-Socket ItemsResulting Effect
LaserLaser Amplifier (Amp)Boosts base damage and critical hit stats
Shield CoreShield CellBoosts shield capacity and recharge rate
EngineThrusterBoosts engine speed and multipliers
Hybrid GeneratorShield Cell OR ThrusterBoosts shield capacity, recharge rate, or speed
DroneLaser or Shield, in each of its slots (a Master Drone has two)A laser adds its damage to your volley; a shield counts as one in a core slot (100% of its stats)

Ammo Management

Laser Ammo is a consumable resource.

  • Ammo stacks in your inventory.
  • You can change active laser ammo via your HUD hotbar.
  • Higher quality ammo provides damage multipliers (e.g., standard x1, advanced plasma x2, ultra core x3, experimental fusion core x4). The Siphon Battery deals x1 damage to shields only and gives it to yours.

invite-friends.title: Invite Friends
invite-friends.html:
Every pilot has one personal invite code. A friend who is new to the game uses it once and gets a starter pack; when that friend reaches level 5, you collect a Thulium reward, and more as more of your friends get there. It is all on one page: Community › Invite Friends.

Your Code

  • Open Community › Invite Friends to see your code, written like BCDF-GHJK. It is made the first time you look and is yours for good: it never changes, and nobody else sees it.
  • Copy code puts the code in your clipboard; Copy invite message puts a short text in it, ready to paste to a friend: the game's name, your code and where to enter it (and, outside Steam, where to get the game). In the Steam build the message leaves the download address out.
  • You can type a code in upper or lower case, with or without the hyphen.

What a Friend Gets

A friend enters your code under Community › Invite Friends (the page shows a Have a code from a friend? card to any pilot who can still use one) and gets, at once and in one go:

Starter pack
Credits100,000
Thulium5,000
N.I.K.E.1
Quantum Laser 21
Engine II1
Advanced Plasma1,000

The pack goes into the friend's hangar. Advanced Plasma is the x2 ammo. If any part of it cannot be given, none is, and the game says to try again later.

Who Can Use a Code

The code is for new accounts, and the game keeps it that way:

  • Level 4 or lower. A pilot at level 5 or above cannot use a code.
  • Once per account. An account that used a code cannot use another.
  • Never your own code.
  • Three per network address per day. From one network address (a household, a school, a mobile carrier's shared address) at most 3 codes can be used in any 24 hours. The page says so when a network has used its share; try again tomorrow or from another network.
  • No guessing. Ten codes nobody has, typed within ten minutes, and the game asks you to wait.

A friend who cannot use a code is told why, in plain words, under the field.

When a Friend Reaches Level 5

When a friend who used your code reaches level 5 (160,000 experience), a reward of 2,500 Thulium waits for you in the list of friends, with a Collect button next to the friend. It is never paid by itself: you collect it, once per friend, whenever you like, even if the friend's account is gone by then.

A friend shows one of three states, in words as well as colour:

  • Joined: used your code.
  • Reached level 5: the reward waits for you.
  • Collected: you have collected it.

The Invite Friends entry in the sidebar's Community group carries a small (!) while something waits to be collected, and so does Return to Base in flight.

Milestones

Friends who reach level 5 also count toward a ladder. Each milestone is paid once, in any order, when you collect it:

Friends at level 5Reward
35,000 Thulium
510,000 Thulium
1025,000 Thulium
2575,000 Thulium

A milestone shows Locked (with how many friends are still missing), Ready (with a Collect button) or Collected. Only friends who reached level 5 count, not those who only used the code, and a friend who reached it stays counted for good.

Good to Know

  • The season's wipe does not touch codes, friends or what you collected.
  • The rewards and the milestones are set on the game server and may change in an update; the page always shows the ones in force.
  • A game server from before Invite Friends has no such page: the section says so.
  • Friends you invite can join your Clan or your Group like any other pilot.

quests.title: Quests
quests.html:
Missions are the main way to level up. Mission Control hands them out: every mission comes from an officer of your own company (if you change company, the officers become your new company's, and the rival x-4 tasks follow it), and each pays experience, credits, Thulium and honor when you claim it. There are 88 missions for levels 1 to 8, eleven a level, and together they carry you from a fresh Protos to the frontline of the PvP centre. Ten Station missions teach you the Skylab and pay you for building it up, and from pilot level 3 a separate line of fifty very hard Challenge missions pays large rewards. Station and Challenge missions pay like the level missions: the numbers in the tables are the base, and your world, boosters and clan boosts multiply them (Rewards).

Most missions are no longer "destroy so many of these": they are short chains. You destroy a few aliens, fly to a point, stay in a sector for some minutes, or find an item and drive it home to Mission Control. Some add a rule: lose no more than so many hull points, or do not die.

In one minute

  • Take them at Mission Control. You can run 5 level missions at once, plus 3 Station missions and 3 Challenge missions.
  • Chains. The steps of a mission with an In order tag open one after the other, and only the open step counts.
  • Four kinds of step besides kills. A quest item that drops only for you and that you drive to Mission Control, a point to visit, a stay of some minutes in a sector and, from season day 4, a swarm to hunt.
  • Conditions. A step or a whole mission may say "hull loss at most N points" or "no death". Break it and that step, or the mission, starts again. Nothing is lost for good.
  • The Challenge line. Fifty very hard missions in five tiers of ten, from pilot level 3. Tier I pays 9,355,000 credits, 70,125 Thulium and 435,500 XP in all, as base values: they pay like a level mission (Rewards).
  • Reworked in 0.4.10. 64 of the level missions are new versions. If you had done one, it is offered again, with its full reward (details).

Mission Control

  • Open Mission Control from the toolbar inside a station's safe zone, or click the Mission Control bubble above the station in your base sector (it follows the station on the map, so fly or zoom out until the station is in view). The Normal Missions tab lists your missions by level, the Challenges tab holds the Challenge line, and Completed Missions holds the ones waiting for you to claim their reward.
  • Accept a mission to start it. You can run 5 missions at once; the Station missions have 3 slots of their own and the Challenge missions 3 more. The mission you accepted last is the one you're tracking (a Station mission only when you track nothing and none of your missions is one that flying can advance): it shows in the Active Quests window, and kills and flight count toward it first. Pick another with the dots in the window's title bar.
  • Some missions must be done in order. They carry an In order tag, and their steps are numbered: see Chained missions.
  • A mission with a quest item, a stay or a condition shows its state live in Active Quests: Carrying with the distance to Mission Control, the time you have stayed, the hull points you have lost (Hull damage: 1,240 / 3,000), Do not die. On the mission's card the same rules show as small pills: Hull limit 3,000 HP, No death, In order, and the clock of a timed mission.
  • Abandon a mission to drop it and its progress. It is back in the list at once, and you can take it again. An item you were carrying for it is gone.
  • A finished mission waits under Completed Missions until you claim it. Claim it whenever you like: the reward doesn't expire.
  • Every mission can be done once per pilot, except the level missions that were reworked in 0.4.10, which are offered once more (see below). Your missions, done and in progress, survive the season's wipe.

Levels

  • Each level from 1 to 8 has ten missions and a Special. A level's missions open when you reach it and stay open at every level above it.
  • Take them in any order. None of the ten waits for another. (The steps inside one mission may have an order.)
  • Every level has the same mix: three missions with a quest item, two that send you to points on the map, two that make you stay in a sector and three plain hunts. A mission has one to four steps, and a hunt asks for one kind of alien or for several.
  • The missions of a level pay 85% of the experience to the next level. The aliens they have you destroy pay the rest, and at low levels quite a bit more: you usually reach the next level before a set is finished.

Special missions

  • The eleventh mission of each level is its Special. It is locked until all ten of the level's other missions are done (claimed, or waiting for their claim), and its card says how many you have left.
  • Specials pay more experience than any other mission of their level, and items besides: lasers, shield parts, generators, Power Cores, Ship Fragments, ammo and booster time.
  • The Specials of levels 3 and 4, Hive Breaker and Hive Purge, are swarm hunts: they open from season day 4.
  • Level 1's regular missions also give a small starter item each: a Light Shield Core, a Repair Drone, a Damage Amp, an Absorption Shield Cell I, some ammo and a stack of rockets to try each kind (Lancet I, Rivet I, Ember I and Scatter I, and Lancet II from the Special).

Chained missions

A chain is a mission whose steps go in a fixed order. It carries an In order tag on its card and in Active Quests. Its steps are numbered: a done step is checked, the highlighted step is the open one, and the steps after it show a lock until it is done.

  • Only the open step counts. Your kills, your flight and your stay time go to it and to no other. Kills you made before a step opened do not count for it.
  • Why in order? A mission tells a small story ("clear the guards, then take the core home"), and the rules need the order: a quest item can only drop once its step is open, a stay counts from the moment it opens, and the conditions of a step (hull limit, no death) run only while that step is open.
  • Missions without the tag open all their steps at once, in any order. Hold the Gate has a point to reach, a four-minute stay in one stretch and kills of 8 Seekers and 3 Phantasm, all open together, so the kills count whenever you make them while the mission runs, in the stay or out of it.
  • In the tables at the end of this page an arrow ("→") joins the steps of an In order mission, and a semicolon (";") joins steps that open together.

Quest items

A quest item is something you have to bring to Mission Control. It is not an inventory item: it cannot be traded, stored or sold, it is part of the mission. Only you can see it. Other pilots, your group mates too, see nothing.

KindHow you get itExample
A dropEvery kill of the named alien in the named sector may drop it. The table gives the chance a kill ("15% a kill") and the kill that drops it for certain ("for certain at kill 10"). The count starts when the step opens.Combined Operations: the Cargo Pod, from the Seekers of x-1.
A scripted dropNo chance: the named kill, counted from the moment the step opens, always carries it.Nest Raid: the third Phantasm of the nest carries the Nest Core.
A placed itemIt lies at a point of the sector from the moment the step opens.Frontier Defense: the Relay Part at 12,500 / 4,800 in x-2.
  1. Find it. A drop appears where the alien died, for 120 seconds; it blinks in the last 12. If you miss it, the next qualifying kill drops it again at once. You see the item as a cyan beacon in the world (a spinning data core in a ring, with a beam rising from it) and as a cyan diamond on the minimap.
  2. Pick it up. Fly within 200 units of it. A message says it is on board, and Active Quests shows Carrying and the distance to Mission Control.
  3. Drive it home. Fly into the safe zone of your own company's Mission Control: the station of your base sector x-1, the ring of 1,600 units around it. A green ring on the screen and on the minimap shows it. The item is delivered at once and the step is done.

Things that stop the carry:

  • Your ship is destroyed, by an alien or by a pilot: the item is lost, and you can get it again (a placed item is back at its point, a drop comes with the next qualifying kill). Nobody can steal it: a pilot who destroys you gets nothing from it.
  • A passed hull limit or a no death rule fails the carry the same way: see Conditions.
  • The Jump CPU and the Base CPU refuse to work while you carry an item. Fly home through the gates. Gates, the cloak and Shield Surge are free to use.
  • If you leave the game you keep carrying when you come back. A drop that was standing on the map is gone, and the next qualifying kill drops it again.
  • Items are only ever in the company sectors x-1 to x-4, never in the Danger Sectors.
  • In a group every mate who counts for the kill (see Where it counts) and has the mission rolls and sees their own item. Nobody can give, take or share one.

Tip

Plan the way home before you pick the item up. From x-3 or x-4 it is two gate jumps to x-1, from x-2 one. Mend first if your hull is low (a destroyed ship loses the item) and keep out of fights on the way: repairs do not give hull-limit points back.

Visit and stay

Visit a point. A visit step names a point of a sector as two numbers, "9,000 / 4,500". They are the same numbers the title bar of the minimap shows for your own ship, so you can steer by them. Fly within 400 units of the point and it counts at once; you do not have to stop (a tour that ends at Mission Control ends inside the station's safe zone). The point is a gold ring on the screen and a gold diamond on the minimap.

Stay in a sector. A stay step asks for some minutes in a sector. It counts only while all three are true:

  • you are on the sector the step names;
  • you are outside every safe zone (a station's or a gate's ring: time in a ring does not count);
  • your ship is active: it has flown 300 units or fired a shot in the last 30 seconds. A parked ship earns nothing.

There are two kinds. A stay that adds up keeps what you have: leave, die, come back, and the minutes are still there. A stay in one stretch starts again from zero when you die, jump or leave the sector (time in a ring or standing still only pauses it), and a toast says so.

Stays and visits do not compete: every open one counts at once, whatever else you are doing. Kills are different: a kill counts for one level mission only (see Where it counts).

Note

Visits and stays may lead into the Danger Sectors (Centre Recon, Centre Vigil and Centre Hold do), where other companies' pilots can attack you. Quest items never do.

Swarm missions

Thirteen missions ask for the ships of the swarms. Two are level Specials: Hive Breaker (level 3: 3 Boss Seekers, 12 Seeker Slaves and 6 Phantasm) and Hive Purge (level 4: 3 Boss Seekers, 12 Seeker Slaves, 2 Bulwarks and a point to visit). Eleven are in the Challenge line: Boss Seekers and Pirate Scouts (Hive Cull, Scout Cull, Hive Culling II, Scout Culling II), Pirate Bosses (Pirate Reckoning, Pirate Bane, Pirate Doom, Pirate Throne) and the Dormant Force (Dormant Dawn, Dormant Dusk, Dormant Dominion).

  • They open on season day 4, the day the swarms appear (30-day schedule). Before it Mission Control refuses them with "This mission opens on season day 4".
  • A swarm ship counts under its own name: a Boss Seeker or a Seeker Slave is no Seeker, a Pirate Scout is no Phantasm.
  • The step names no sector, because the swarms roam: the Seeker Swarm in x-1 and x-2, the Pirate Swarm in x-2 and x-3, the Dormant Swarm in the Danger Sectors. A Boss Seeker or a Pirate Boss comes back 2 minutes after it falls.
  • The Dormant missions are for a crew: there is one Dormant Swarm in each world, and a group of strong ships takes it (how the fight goes). The next tier does not wait for Dormant Dawn or Dormant Dusk (the Challenge line).
  • A Boss Seeker hits harder than a new pilot's ship can bear: read how the fight goes before you start.

Conditions

A condition is an extra rule on one step or on a whole mission. There are two. The tables write them as "(hull loss at most 3,000 points)" and "(no death)"; a condition on the whole mission reads "(whole mission: ...)".

  • Hull limit. Lose no more than so many hull points. The count is the hull you really lose: the points the hull bar falls by, after your shield and absorbance have taken their share. Damage to the shield does not count, black-hole radiation does, and repairs give nothing back. A killing blow always passes the limit.
  • No death. If your ship is destroyed, the condition breaks.

When the clock runs. A limit on a whole mission counts from the moment you accept it (and from every restart) until the mission is done. A limit on a step counts from the moment the step opens; for a carried item, from the pick-up to the delivery. It counts every hull point you lose in that time, whoever hits you, and in a mission whose steps are open together that includes the fights of its other steps.

What a broken condition does. Nothing is lost for good, no Thulium is charged and the mission stays active. A message tells you ("condition broken. The attempt starts again.").

What carries the conditionWhat happens when it breaks
A kill stepThe kills of that step go back to 0. The other steps keep their progress.
A carried itemThe carry fails and you fetch the item again (see Quest items).
A visit or a stay stepThe step starts again.
A whole missionEvery step starts again, a carried item is lost, and the clock of a timed mission keeps running.

Dying breaks a hull limit that is running as well as a no-death rule.

The limits are set in points, for the ship you fly at that level. A carried item's limit is 3,000 hull points on levels 1 to 3, 17,000 on levels 4 to 6 and 46,000 on levels 7 and 8; stays and tours that run longer have larger numbers. They are the same in every world, so in Beta and Gamma, where the aliens hit harder, they leave you less room. Check the mission's card before you accept. A limit may also be given as a percent of your ship's hull, and the stricter one counts when both are given; every mission of this release uses points.

Mission examples

Eight missions from the real list, from the first hour to the Challenge line. Their numbers are in the tables at the end of this page; every pay named here is the base (see Rewards).

  • Beacon Watch (level 1). Fly to the point 9,000 / 4,500 in x-1, then stay 5 minutes in x-1. The whole mission is no death: if your ship is destroyed, you begin again at the beacon. Keep moving or shooting, or the minutes do not count. Pays 700 XP, 3,500 credits, 5 Thulium, 7 honor and a Repair Drone I.
  • Combined Operations (level 1). Destroy 8 Seekers in x-1, then find the Cargo Pod: every Seeker you destroy there after that has a 15% chance to carry it, and the 10th is sure. Bring it to Mission Control with a hull loss of at most 3,000 points. Pays 1,550 XP, 8,000 credits, Advanced Plasma and Ember I.
  • Hold the Gate (level 2, 15 minutes, no death). Four steps open at once: reach the point 12,500 / 2,500 in x-2, stay 4 minutes in one stretch there, and destroy 8 Seekers and 3 Phantasm. The kills count whenever you make them while the mission runs. Die, and everything starts again, but the clock does not.
  • Nest Raid (level 3). Destroy 7 Phantasm in x-3, fly to the nest at 7,500 / 7,600, then destroy Phantasm until the third one drops the Nest Core: it is scripted, the third kill always carries it. Bring it home with a hull loss of at most 3,000 points and without losing your ship. Pays 4,500 XP and 36,000 credits.
  • Heavy Courier (level 4, 40 minutes). Destroy 10 Phantasm in x-3, reach the points 13,400 / 5,000 and 13,600 / 1,900, then take the Manifest from a Bulwark (25% a kill, sure at the 5th) and carry it to Mission Control with a hull loss of at most 17,000 points and no death. Pays 10,500 XP, 52,000 credits and 315 Thulium.
  • Hive Breaker (level 3 Special, from season day 4). Destroy 3 Boss Seekers and 12 Seeker Slaves, in any sector, and 6 Phantasm in x-3, in any order. Pays 6,800 XP, 54,500 credits, 170 Thulium, a Quantum Laser 2, 10 Ship Fragments and 200 Ultra Core.
  • Grand Tour (level 8, 25 minutes, no death). Fly to 8,000 / 4,500 in x-4, then to 6,000 / 4,500 in the centre, destroy 2 Goombahs in a rival company's x-4 and fly to its heart at 8,000 / 4,500. The ring gates and the centre both lead there. Pays 66,000 XP, 165,000 credits and 1,320 Thulium.
  • Untouched (Challenge). Destroy 25 Phantasm in x-3 in a row while losing no more than 39,000 hull points. Go over the limit and the count goes back to 0. Pays, at base, 44,000 XP, 855,000 credits, 6,405 Thulium, 2,370 honor, an Ancient Control Unit and 5 hours of Shield Wall II.

Station missions

  • Ten missions about your Skylab, in a Station section at the top of the Missions page. The first, Light the Station, is open from level 1 and tells you where the Skylab is: Menu, Economy, Skylab. The station menu's Skylab row pulses until you have taken it or built Solar.
  • They are taken, tracked, abandoned and claimed like every mission, but they don't count in the 5: you can run 3 Station missions at once besides your other 5. A Station mission can wait for hours of upgrade timers and never holds up a combat mission.
  • Taking a Station mission doesn't change the mission you're tracking when you have one that flying can advance: the Active Quests window keeps showing your combat mission, and the Station mission is a dot in its title bar (hover it for its progress, click it to show it).
  • Each opens at its own pilot level and after the Station missions it follows (claimed first): a locked card says which. The first three open at level 1. The last, Core Ten, takes the Core to level 10, the level that opens the Skylab's Research Centre.
  • Their tasks read your Skylab: build a module or raise it to a level (done while the module is at that level or higher; no module goes above your Core, so a Solar goal can need the Core raised first), and collect credits from the Credit Farm (counted from the moment you accept the mission, with the Collect Resources button). A mission whose tasks are all true at once is done: one you already meet when you accept it is done at once.
  • The Credit Farm costs nothing to build, so First Farm pays you 3,000 Credits and 100 Thulium for building it. Collecting takes time: Payday asks for 1,000 Credits, about two hours of a level 1 farm (500 an hour), and Fifty Thousand asks for 50,000, about 33 hours of the level 3 farm that Growing Season leaves you (1,500 an hour).
  • Solar makes only 25% of its power while it upgrades, so a station with a Thulium Farm stops its farms until the upgrade is done (see Solar Module). Brighter Panels (Solar to level 3: 5 and 15 minutes; the small station of that mission still fits), Growing Season (the step to level 5 takes 45 minutes) and Open the Supply Line (Solar to level 6: 60 minutes) tell you how long it lasts.
  • They pay like a level mission. The numbers in the table are the base: your world's bonus, boosters, Premium XP and your clan's Credits and Thulium boosts multiply them (Rewards). A Station mission has no world of its own, so it pays the world you fly in when you claim it. It gives no items. Their base experience is on top of the 85% the levels' missions pay (at most 5% of a level's gap).
  • Station missions don't count toward the Wipe Points for missions done. They survive the wipe like every mission, and so does what you built.

The Challenge line

From pilot level 3, the Challenges tab of Mission Control opens a second line: fifty very hard missions in five tiers of ten, for the pilots who want more than the levels give. Every tier asks for more than the one before, and all fifty are in the game. The tables at the end of this page list every mission and every number.

  • Ten in any order. The ten missions of a tier are open together. Tier II opens when you have claimed all ten of tier I, and tier III when you have claimed all ten of tier II. Tiers IV and V open when you have claimed nine of the ten before them: Dormant Dawn (tier III) and Dormant Dusk (tier IV) are missions of the Dormant Swarm, which needs a crew, so they are optional.
  • Three at once, besides your 5 level missions and 3 Station missions.
  • They pay like a level mission. The reward in the tables is the base, paid once: your world's bonus, boosters, Premium XP and your clan's Credits and Thulium boosts multiply it, as Rewards explains with an example. Honor is paid in tier I only. They survive the wipe, and they do not count for the Wipe Points of missions.
  • Kills count twice. A kill counts for every Challenge mission that asks for it and for the one level mission it counts for, so a thousand-kill mission never starves your level missions.
  • Groups. A kill counts for the pilot who is paid for it and for every group mate within 4,000 units of the wreck who fired a laser or a rocket in the last 15 seconds. Each pilot keeps their own count.
  • Stays need shots, except in the centre. A stay in x-3, in x-4 or in a rival's x-4 counts only while you have fired a shot in the last 60 seconds, so a parked or circling ship earns nothing. The stays in the Danger Sectors (Centre Watch, Rim Vigil, Last Watch), where no alien lives, count a ship that has flown 300 units or fired in the last 30 seconds, as the stays of the level missions do.

Time limits

  • Some missions are timed. Mission Control shows the limit on the mission's card before you accept it (a clock and "15 min"), and once you accept it a countdown runs on the card and in Active Quests. It turns amber in the last minute and red when time is up.
  • A timed mission that runs out fails: it leaves your active missions and you can accept it again at once, from the start.
  • The limits in the tables below are Alpha's. Beta's aliens are 1.5 times as strong and Gamma's twice, so their limits are 1.5 and 2 times as long. The clock is set when you accept the mission, for the world you're in.
  • Steps have no time limit of their own: the mission's limit covers all of them. A broken condition restarts a step or the mission, but it never resets the clock.

Rewards

  • Experience, credits, Thulium and honor are multiplied by the world the mission was done in: 1x in Alpha, 2x in Beta, 3x in Gamma. Your boosters (the Experience Kit, the Honor Beacon) add to them, and premium doubles the experience. The Thulium and credits boosts of your clan add to the credits and the Thulium of every mission you claim: level, Station and Challenge.
  • Station and Challenge missions pay like level missions. The numbers printed in their tables are the base. A Challenge mission is paid by the world you did it in, like a level mission (the lowest one, should it span two). A Station mission has no world of its own: it pays the world you fly in when you claim it.
  • An example. Seeker Plague (Challenge) has a base of 1,100,000 credits, 8,260 Thulium, 31,500 XP and 3,060 honor. Done and claimed in Gamma with nothing switched on, it pays 3,300,000 credits, 24,780 Thulium, 94,500 XP and 9,180 honor. With your clan's Credits and Thulium boosts at their top (+10% each) it pays 3,630,000 credits and 27,258 Thulium.
  • The clan bank cap. However big a claim is, a pilot can send at most 1,000,000 credits into clans in any 24 hours.
  • Items and booster time are the same in every world. Items go to your inventory, booster hours add to what the booster has left, and ammo is ready to fire even if you claim while flying.

The reworked missions

Update 0.4.10 reworked the level missions into chains. 64 of the 88 are new versions; the 24 that stayed as they were are the plain kill missions (like Basic Training: Combat) and the Specials of levels 1, 2 and 5 to 8.

If you had done one of the 64, you do the new version too. At your first flight after the update a System line tells you: "Mission Control has new missions: the level quests were reworked."

  • The mission is offered again. It is back in Mission Control, and it pays its full reward again: experience, credits, Thulium, honor and items, by the world you do it in.
  • A Special locks again until the level's regular missions are done again, so level 3's ten missions come before Hive Breaker once more.
  • A reward you had not claimed yet is paid as before (the larger of the old and the new reward), and then the new version is offered.
  • A mission you had running is carried over to its new steps by the share you had done. A visit counts only when its share is whole, and a quest item is never handed in by that conversion.
  • Nothing goes down. Your level, your statistics and your Wipe Points stay. A mission you do again does not count for the Wipe Points a second time: it was counted the first time.
  • The Station missions, the Challenge line and the 24 missions that stayed are not touched.

Danger

The higher sectors are where the missions pay, and where you can die. Plan your kit for them:

  • PvP: other companies' pilots can attack you in x-4 and the centre in every world, from x-2 up in Beta, and everywhere in Gamma (except in safe zones and during the Peace Protocol). The ring gates bring other companies' pilots into your x-3 too: in Beta and Gamma one of them can destroy you there while you carry an item.
  • Bulwarks (x-3, x-4) outrun a Protos and hit hard. Fight them from an Ostirion, near a gate's safe zone, and pull back into it to repair.
  • Goombahs (x-3, x-4) have a range of 800, hit for 3,000 and never start a fight: leave one alone and it leaves you alone, shoot it and it turns on you until 10 seconds after your last hit (and it mends when left alone). A ship whose lasers are all Starfire-3 (range 850) outranges them and Bulwarks alike: with a ship faster than they are (an Ostirion or above; a Goombah flies 180, a Bulwark 175) you can fire without taking a hit. Your ship's range is the average of its lasers' ranges, so a Starfire-3 beside two Quantum Laser 2 fires from 750: far enough to keep away from a Bulwark (700), not from a Goombah (800). Level 5's Special gives you one; you can also make one in Assembly, from Velkonite Reinforced Plates that the Forgery of your Skylab makes.
  • Crystalys roam the border (x-4). Nothing in reach of level 8 outranges one, and only a fast ship outruns it: keep your distance, and watch the minimap.
  • When you are destroyed you choose where to come back: at your base, at the nearest portal or on the spot (see Dying and Coming Back). A timed mission's clock keeps running meanwhile, a carried item is lost, and a no-death rule breaks.

The missions

The time limits are Alpha's ("–": none). "→" joins the steps of an In order mission, which must be done in that order; steps joined by ";" open together and can be done in any order. A condition written after a step belongs to that step, "(whole mission: ...)" to every step.

A quest item reads "may drop it: 15% a kill, for certain at kill 10": every kill of that alien in that sector rolls the chance, and the 10th kill since the step opened drops it for sure. "From season day 4" is a swarm hunt.

quests.markdown:
# Quests

Missions are the main way to level up. Mission Control hands them out: every mission comes from an officer of your own company (if you [change company](/wiki/01-General/Getting-Started.md#changing-your-company), the officers become your new company's, and the `rival x-4` tasks follow it), and each pays experience, credits, Thulium and honor when you claim it. There are **88 missions for levels 1 to 8**, eleven a level, and together they carry you from a fresh Protos to the frontline of the PvP centre. Ten **Station missions** teach you the [Skylab](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Skylab.md) and pay you for building it up, and from pilot level 3 a separate line of fifty very hard **Challenge missions** pays large rewards. Station and Challenge missions pay like the level missions: the numbers in the tables are the **base**, and your world, boosters and clan boosts multiply them ([Rewards](#rewards)).

Most missions are no longer "destroy so many of these": they are short **chains**. You destroy a few aliens, fly to a point, stay in a sector for some minutes, or find an item and drive it home to Mission Control. Some add a rule: lose no more than so many hull points, or do not die.

## In one minute

- **Take them at Mission Control.** You can run 5 level missions at once, plus 3 Station missions and 3 Challenge missions.
- **Chains.** The steps of a mission with an **In order** tag open one after the other, and only the open step counts.
- **Four kinds of step besides kills.** A **quest item** that drops only for you and that you drive to Mission Control, a **point to visit**, a **stay** of some minutes in a sector and, from season day 4, a **swarm** to hunt.
- **Conditions.** A step or a whole mission may say "hull loss at most N points" or "no death". Break it and that step, or the mission, starts again. Nothing is lost for good.
- **The Challenge line.** Fifty very hard missions in five tiers of ten, from pilot level 3. Tier I pays 9,355,000 credits, 70,125 Thulium and 435,500 XP in all, as base values: they pay like a level mission ([Rewards](#rewards)).
- **Reworked in 0.4.10.** 64 of the level missions are new versions. If you had done one, it is offered again, with its full reward ([details](#reworked-missions)).

## Mission Control



- Open **Mission Control** from the toolbar inside a station's safe zone, or click the **Mission Control** bubble above the station in your base sector (it follows the station on the map, so fly or zoom out until the station is in view). The **Normal Missions** tab lists your missions by level, the **Challenges** tab holds the [Challenge line](#challenge-line), and **Completed Missions** holds the ones waiting for you to claim their reward.
- **Accept** a mission to start it. You can run **5 missions at once**; the [Station missions](#station-missions) have 3 slots of their own and the [Challenge missions](#challenge-line) 3 more. The mission you accepted last is the one you're **tracking** (a Station mission only when you track nothing and none of your missions is one that flying can advance): it shows in the **Active Quests** window, and kills and flight count toward it first. Pick another with the dots in the window's title bar.
- Some missions must be done **in order**. They carry an **In order** tag, and their steps are numbered: see [Chained missions](#chained-missions).
- A mission with a quest item, a stay or a condition shows its state live in Active Quests: **Carrying** with the distance to Mission Control, the time you have stayed, the hull points you have lost (**Hull damage: 1,240 / 3,000**), **Do not die**. On the mission's card the same rules show as small pills: **Hull limit 3,000 HP**, **No death**, **In order**, and the clock of a timed mission.
- **Abandon** a mission to drop it and its progress. It is back in the list at once, and you can take it again. An item you were carrying for it is gone.
- A finished mission waits under **Completed Missions** until you **claim** it. Claim it whenever you like: the reward doesn't expire.
- Every mission can be done **once per pilot**, except the level missions that were reworked in 0.4.10, which are offered once more ([see below](#reworked-missions)). Your missions, done and in progress, survive the season's wipe.

## Levels

- Each level from 1 to 8 has **ten missions and a Special**. A level's missions open when you reach it and stay open at every level above it.
- **Take them in any order.** None of the ten waits for another. (The steps inside one mission may have an order.)
- Every level has the same mix: **three** missions with a quest item, **two** that send you to points on the map, **two** that make you stay in a sector and **three** plain hunts. A mission has one to four steps, and a hunt asks for one kind of alien or for several.
- The missions of a level pay **85% of the experience** to the next level. The aliens they have you destroy pay the rest, and at low levels quite a bit more: you usually reach the next level before a set is finished.

## Special missions

- The eleventh mission of each level is its **Special**. It is locked until **all ten** of the level's other missions are done (claimed, or waiting for their claim), and its card says how many you have left.
- Specials pay more experience than any other mission of their level, and **items** besides: lasers, shield parts, generators, Power Cores, Ship Fragments, ammo and booster time.
- The Specials of levels 3 and 4, **Hive Breaker** and **Hive Purge**, are [swarm hunts](#swarm-missions): they open from season day 4.
- Level 1's regular missions also give a small starter item each: a Light Shield Core, a Repair Drone, a Damage Amp, an Absorption Shield Cell I, some ammo and a stack of rockets to try each kind (Lancet I, Rivet I, Ember I and Scatter I, and Lancet II from the Special).

## Chained missions

A **chain** is a mission whose steps go in a fixed order. It carries an **In order** tag on its card and in Active Quests. Its steps are numbered: a done step is checked, the **highlighted** step is the open one, and the steps after it show a lock until it is done.

- **Only the open step counts.** Your kills, your flight and your stay time go to it and to no other. Kills you made before a step opened do not count for it.
- **Why in order?** A mission tells a small story ("clear the guards, then take the core home"), and the rules need the order: a quest item can only drop once its step is open, a stay counts from the moment it opens, and the conditions of a step (hull limit, no death) run only while that step is open.
- **Missions without the tag open all their steps at once**, in any order. **Hold the Gate** has a point to reach, a four-minute stay in one stretch and kills of 8 Seekers and 3 Phantasm, all open together, so the kills count whenever you make them while the mission runs, in the stay or out of it.
- In the tables at the end of this page an arrow ("→") joins the steps of an In order mission, and a semicolon (";") joins steps that open together.

## Quest items

A quest item is something you have to bring to Mission Control. It is not an inventory item: it cannot be traded, stored or sold, it is part of the mission. **Only you can see it.** Other pilots, your group mates too, see nothing.

| Kind | How you get it | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A drop** | Every kill of the named alien in the named sector may drop it. The table gives the chance a kill ("15% a kill") and the kill that drops it for certain ("for certain at kill 10"). The count starts when the step opens. | Combined Operations: the Cargo Pod, from the Seekers of `x-1`. |
| **A scripted drop** | No chance: the named kill, counted from the moment the step opens, always carries it. | Nest Raid: the third Phantasm of the nest carries the Nest Core. |
| **A placed item** | It lies at a point of the sector from the moment the step opens. | Frontier Defense: the Relay Part at 12,500 / 4,800 in `x-2`. |

1. **Find it.** A drop appears where the alien died, for **120 seconds**; it blinks in the last 12. If you miss it, the next qualifying kill drops it again at once. You see the item as a cyan beacon in the world (a spinning data core in a ring, with a beam rising from it) and as a cyan diamond on the minimap.
2. **Pick it up.** Fly within **200 units** of it. A message says it is on board, and Active Quests shows **Carrying** and the distance to Mission Control.
3. **Drive it home.** Fly into the safe zone of **your own company's** Mission Control: the station of your base sector `x-1`, the ring of 1,600 units around it. A green ring on the screen and on the minimap shows it. The item is delivered at once and the step is done.

Things that stop the carry:

- **Your ship is destroyed**, by an alien or by a pilot: the item is lost, and you can get it again (a placed item is back at its point, a drop comes with the next qualifying kill). Nobody can steal it: a pilot who destroys you gets nothing from it.
- **A passed hull limit** or a **no death** rule fails the carry the same way: see [Conditions](#conditions).
- **The Jump CPU and the Base CPU refuse to work while you carry an item.** Fly home through the gates. Gates, the cloak and Shield Surge are free to use.
- If you leave the game you keep carrying when you come back. A drop that was standing on the map is gone, and the next qualifying kill drops it again.
- Items are only ever in the company sectors `x-1` to `x-4`, **never in the Danger Sectors**.
- In a [group](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Groups.md) every mate who counts for the kill (see [Where it counts](#where-it-counts)) and has the mission rolls and sees their own item. Nobody can give, take or share one.

> [!TIP]
> Plan the way home before you pick the item up. From `x-3` or `x-4` it is two gate jumps to `x-1`, from `x-2` one. Mend first if your hull is low (a destroyed ship loses the item) and keep out of fights on the way: repairs do not give hull-limit points back.

## Visit and stay

**Visit a point.** A visit step names a point of a sector as two numbers, "9,000 / 4,500". They are the same numbers the title bar of the minimap shows for your own ship, so you can steer by them. Fly within **400 units** of the point and it counts at once; you do not have to stop (a tour that ends at Mission Control ends inside the station's safe zone). The point is a **gold ring** on the screen and a gold diamond on the minimap.

**Stay in a sector.** A stay step asks for some minutes in a sector. It counts only while all three are true:

- you are on the sector the step names;
- you are **outside every safe zone** (a station's or a gate's ring: time in a ring does not count);
- your ship is **active**: it has flown 300 units or fired a shot in the last 30 seconds. A parked ship earns nothing.

There are two kinds. A stay that **adds up** keeps what you have: leave, die, come back, and the minutes are still there. A stay **in one stretch** starts again from zero when you die, jump or leave the sector (time in a ring or standing still only pauses it), and a toast says so.

Stays and visits do not compete: every open one counts at once, whatever else you are doing. Kills are different: a kill counts for one level mission only (see [Where it counts](#where-it-counts)).

> [!NOTE]
> Visits and stays may lead into the Danger Sectors (Centre Recon, Centre Vigil and Centre Hold do), where other companies' pilots can attack you. Quest items never do.

## Swarm missions

Thirteen missions ask for the ships of the [swarms](/wiki/05-Swarms/Swarms.md). Two are level Specials: **Hive Breaker** (level 3: 3 Boss Seekers, 12 Seeker Slaves and 6 Phantasm) and **Hive Purge** (level 4: 3 Boss Seekers, 12 Seeker Slaves, 2 Bulwarks and a point to visit). Eleven are in the Challenge line: Boss Seekers and Pirate Scouts (**Hive Cull**, **Scout Cull**, **Hive Culling II**, **Scout Culling II**), Pirate Bosses (**Pirate Reckoning**, **Pirate Bane**, **Pirate Doom**, **Pirate Throne**) and the Dormant Force (**Dormant Dawn**, **Dormant Dusk**, **Dormant Dominion**).

- **They open on season day 4**, the day the swarms appear ([30-day schedule](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Wipe-Timeline.md#30-day-season-schedule)). Before it Mission Control refuses them with "This mission opens on season day 4".
- A swarm ship counts under **its own name**: a Boss Seeker or a Seeker Slave is no Seeker, a Pirate Scout is no Phantasm.
- The step names no sector, because the swarms roam: the [Seeker Swarm](/wiki/05-Swarms/Seeker-Swarm.md) in `x-1` and `x-2`, the [Pirate Swarm](/wiki/05-Swarms/Pirate-Swarm.md) in `x-2` and `x-3`, the [Dormant Swarm](/wiki/05-Swarms/Dormant-Swarm.md) in the Danger Sectors. A Boss Seeker or a Pirate Boss comes back 2 minutes after it falls.
- The Dormant missions are for a crew: there is one Dormant Swarm in each world, and a group of strong ships takes it ([how the fight goes](/wiki/05-Swarms/Dormant-Swarm.md#how-the-fight-goes)). The next tier does not wait for **Dormant Dawn** or **Dormant Dusk** ([the Challenge line](#challenge-line)).
- A Boss Seeker hits harder than a new pilot's ship can bear: read [how the fight goes](/wiki/05-Swarms/Seeker-Swarm.md#how-the-fight-goes) before you start.

## Conditions

A **condition** is an extra rule on one step or on a whole mission. There are two. The tables write them as "(hull loss at most 3,000 points)" and "(no death)"; a condition on the whole mission reads "(whole mission: ...)".

- **Hull limit.** Lose no more than so many **hull points**. The count is the hull you really lose: the points the hull bar falls by, after your shield and absorbance have taken their share. Damage to the shield does not count, black-hole radiation does, and repairs give nothing back. A killing blow always passes the limit.
- **No death.** If your ship is destroyed, the condition breaks.

**When the clock runs.** A limit on a whole mission counts from the moment you accept it (and from every restart) until the mission is done. A limit on a step counts from the moment the step opens; for a carried item, from the pick-up to the delivery. It counts every hull point you lose in that time, whoever hits you, and in a mission whose steps are open together that includes the fights of its other steps.

**What a broken condition does.** Nothing is lost for good, no Thulium is charged and the mission stays active. A message tells you ("condition broken. The attempt starts again.").

| What carries the condition | What happens when it breaks |
| :--- | :--- |
| A kill step | The kills of that step go back to 0. The other steps keep their progress. |
| A carried item | The carry fails and you fetch the item again (see [Quest items](#quest-items)). |
| A visit or a stay step | The step starts again. |
| A whole mission | Every step starts again, a carried item is lost, and the clock of a timed mission keeps running. |

Dying breaks a hull limit that is running as well as a no-death rule.

The limits are set in points, for the ship you fly at that level. A carried item's limit is 3,000 hull points on levels 1 to 3, 17,000 on levels 4 to 6 and 46,000 on levels 7 and 8; stays and tours that run longer have larger numbers. They are the same in every world, so in Beta and Gamma, where the aliens hit harder, they leave you less room. Check the mission's card before you accept. A limit may also be given as a percent of your ship's hull, and the stricter one counts when both are given; every mission of this release uses points.

## Mission examples

Eight missions from the real list, from the first hour to the Challenge line. Their numbers are in the tables at the end of this page; every pay named here is the **base** (see [Rewards](#rewards)).

- **Beacon Watch** (level 1). Fly to the point 9,000 / 4,500 in `x-1`, then stay 5 minutes in `x-1`. The whole mission is **no death**: if your ship is destroyed, you begin again at the beacon. Keep moving or shooting, or the minutes do not count. Pays 700 XP, 3,500 credits, 5 Thulium, 7 honor and a Repair Drone I.
- **Combined Operations** (level 1). Destroy 8 Seekers in `x-1`, then find the Cargo Pod: every Seeker you destroy there after that has a 15% chance to carry it, and the 10th is sure. Bring it to Mission Control with a hull loss of at most 3,000 points. Pays 1,550 XP, 8,000 credits, Advanced Plasma and Ember I.
- **Hold the Gate** (level 2, 15 minutes, no death). Four steps open at once: reach the point 12,500 / 2,500 in `x-2`, stay 4 minutes in one stretch there, and destroy 8 Seekers and 3 Phantasm. The kills count whenever you make them while the mission runs. Die, and everything starts again, but the clock does not.
- **Nest Raid** (level 3). Destroy 7 Phantasm in `x-3`, fly to the nest at 7,500 / 7,600, then destroy Phantasm until the third one drops the Nest Core: it is scripted, the third kill always carries it. Bring it home with a hull loss of at most 3,000 points and without losing your ship. Pays 4,500 XP and 36,000 credits.
- **Heavy Courier** (level 4, 40 minutes). Destroy 10 Phantasm in `x-3`, reach the points 13,400 / 5,000 and 13,600 / 1,900, then take the Manifest from a Bulwark (25% a kill, sure at the 5th) and carry it to Mission Control with a hull loss of at most 17,000 points and no death. Pays 10,500 XP, 52,000 credits and 315 Thulium.
- **Hive Breaker** (level 3 Special, from season day 4). Destroy 3 Boss Seekers and 12 Seeker Slaves, in any sector, and 6 Phantasm in `x-3`, in any order. Pays 6,800 XP, 54,500 credits, 170 Thulium, a Quantum Laser 2, 10 Ship Fragments and 200 Ultra Core.
- **Grand Tour** (level 8, 25 minutes, no death). Fly to 8,000 / 4,500 in `x-4`, then to 6,000 / 4,500 in the centre, destroy 2 Goombahs in a rival company's `x-4` and fly to its heart at 8,000 / 4,500. The [ring gates](/wiki/01-General/Spacemap%20Travel.md#jump-links) and the centre both lead there. Pays 66,000 XP, 165,000 credits and 1,320 Thulium.
- **Untouched** (Challenge). Destroy 25 Phantasm in `x-3` in a row while losing no more than 39,000 hull points. Go over the limit and the count goes back to 0. Pays, at base, 44,000 XP, 855,000 credits, 6,405 Thulium, 2,370 honor, an Ancient Control Unit and 5 hours of Shield Wall II.

## Station missions

- Ten missions about your [Skylab](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Skylab.md), in a **Station** section at the top of the Missions page. The first, **Light the Station**, is open from level 1 and tells you where the Skylab is: Menu, Economy, Skylab. The station menu's Skylab row pulses until you have taken it or built Solar.
- They are taken, tracked, abandoned and claimed like every mission, but they don't count in the 5: you can run **3 Station missions at once** besides your other 5. A Station mission can wait for hours of upgrade timers and never holds up a combat mission.
- Taking a Station mission doesn't change the mission you're tracking when you have one that flying can advance: the Active Quests window keeps showing your combat mission, and the Station mission is a dot in its title bar (hover it for its progress, click it to show it).
- Each opens at its own **pilot level** and after the Station missions it follows (claimed first): a locked card says which. The first three open at level 1. The last, **Core Ten**, takes the Core to level 10, the level that opens the Skylab's [Research Centre](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Research.md).
- Their tasks read your Skylab: **build** a module or **raise it to a level** (done while the module is at that level or higher; no module goes above your Core, so a Solar goal can need the Core raised first), and **collect** credits from the Credit Farm (counted from the moment you accept the mission, with the Collect Resources button). A mission whose tasks are all true at once is done: one you already meet when you accept it is done at once.
- The Credit Farm costs nothing to build, so **First Farm** pays you 3,000 Credits and 100 Thulium for building it. Collecting takes time: **Payday** asks for 1,000 Credits, about two hours of a level 1 farm (500 an hour), and **Fifty Thousand** asks for 50,000, about 33 hours of the level 3 farm that **Growing Season** leaves you (1,500 an hour).
- Solar makes only 25% of its power while it upgrades, so a station with a Thulium Farm stops its farms until the upgrade is done (see [Solar Module](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Skylab.md#solar-module)). **Brighter Panels** (Solar to level 3: 5 and 15 minutes; the small station of that mission still fits), **Growing Season** (the step to level 5 takes 45 minutes) and **Open the Supply Line** (Solar to level 6: 60 minutes) tell you how long it lasts.
- **They pay like a level mission.** The numbers in the table are the **base**: your world's bonus, boosters, Premium XP and your clan's Credits and Thulium boosts multiply them ([Rewards](#rewards)). A Station mission has no world of its own, so it pays the world you fly in when you claim it. It gives no items. Their base experience is on top of the 85% the levels' missions pay (at most 5% of a level's gap).
- Station missions don't count toward the [Wipe Points](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Wipe-Timeline.md) for missions done. They survive the wipe like every mission, and so does what you built.

## The Challenge line {#challenge-line}

From **pilot level 3**, the **Challenges** tab of Mission Control opens a second line: **fifty very hard missions in five tiers of ten**, for the pilots who want more than the levels give. Every tier asks for more than the one before, and all fifty are in the game. [The tables](#challenge-missions-table) at the end of this page list every mission and every number.

- **Ten in any order.** The ten missions of a tier are open together. **Tier II** opens when you have claimed all ten of tier I, and **tier III** when you have claimed all ten of tier II. **Tiers IV and V** open when you have claimed **nine of the ten** before them: **Dormant Dawn** (tier III) and **Dormant Dusk** (tier IV) are missions of the [Dormant Swarm](/wiki/05-Swarms/Dormant-Swarm.md), which needs a crew, so they are optional.
- **Three at once**, besides your 5 level missions and 3 Station missions.
- **They pay like a level mission.** The reward in the tables is the **base**, paid once: your world's bonus, boosters, Premium XP and your clan's Credits and Thulium boosts multiply it, as [Rewards](#rewards) explains with an example. **Honor is paid in tier I only.** They survive the wipe, and they do not count for the Wipe Points of missions.
- **Kills count twice.** A kill counts for every Challenge mission that asks for it **and** for the one level mission it counts for, so a thousand-kill mission never starves your level missions.
- **Groups.** A kill counts for the pilot who is paid for it and for every group mate within **4,000 units** of the wreck who fired a laser or a rocket in the last 15 seconds. Each pilot keeps their own count.
- **Stays need shots, except in the centre.** A stay in `x-3`, in `x-4` or in a rival's `x-4` counts only while you have fired a shot in the last 60 seconds, so a parked or circling ship earns nothing. The stays in the Danger Sectors (**Centre Watch**, **Rim Vigil**, **Last Watch**), where no alien lives, count a ship that has flown 300 units or fired in the last 30 seconds, as the stays of the level missions do.

What each tier asks, with missions from the tables:

- **Tier I, Proving Ground.** The big hunts of the home sectors and the first hard tests: **Seeker Plague** and **Phantasm Tide** (1,000 of each), **Bulwark Wall** (150 Bulwarks), **Untouched** (25 Phantasm in a row, 39,000 hull points at most), two swarm hunts from season day 4 (**Hive Cull**, **Scout Cull**), **Iron Vigil** (45 minutes in one stretch in `x-3`), **Gauntlet of the Centre** (six steps through the centre, no death), **Convoy** and **Hundred in an Hour**.
- **Tier II, Iron Border.** Bigger hunts and longer watches at the border: 2,500 Seekers (**Seeker Blight**), 2,500 Phantasm (**Phantasm Flood**), 400 Bulwarks (**Bulwark Storm**), 100 Goombahs (**Goombah Hunt**), 90 minutes in `x-4` (**Iron Vigil II**) and the first Pirate Bosses.
- **Tier III, The Centre.** The centre and its Goombahs: 250 Goombahs (**Goombah Scourge**), 800 Bulwarks (**Bulwark Blight**), 5,000 Phantasm (**Phantasm Ocean**), 10 Crystalys (**Crystalys Trial**), an hour in the Danger Sectors (**Centre Watch**), a tour of the centre's four corners (**Four Corners**) and a Dormant Force hunt (**Dormant Dawn**).
- **Tier IV, The Abyss.** 50 Crystalys (**Crystalys Purge**), 500 Goombahs (**Goombah Rout**), 2,000 Bulwarks (**Bulwark Sea**), 90 minutes in `DS-4` (**Rim Vigil**), two hours in a rival's `x-4` (**Rival Ground**) and 10 Dormant Force (**Dormant Dusk**).

## Where it counts

Most steps name the sector where they count, and only kills and distance flown **there** count toward them. A visit, a stay and an item name their sector the same way. A few kill steps name none and count in **every** sector: the swarm ships of Hive Breaker and Hive Purge, and the big hunts of the Challenge line (Seeker Plague, Phantasm Tide, Bulwark Wall, Hive Cull, Scout Cull and the big hunts of the tiers after tier I). The Station steps read your Skylab and have no sector either. The sector shows next to a step as one of your own maps:

| In the tables | Means | You see (a Mars pilot) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `x-1` … `x-4` | that sector of any company: yours, or another company's | `M-3` |
| `DS-x` | any sector of the PvP centre, the Danger Sectors `DS-1` to `DS-4` | `DS-x` |
| `rival x-4` | another company's border sector (not yours), a short hop through the ring gates or across the centre | `T-4 · G-4` |

The missions climb the sectors with your level:

| Level | Where you fight | Where it leads |
| --: | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | your base (`x-1`) and second sector (`x-2`) | – |
| 2 | the second sector | a first look through the gate into `x-3` |
| 3 | the third sector (`x-3`), near its gate; a few warm-ups in `x-2` | – |
| 4 | the third sector | a look through the border gate into `x-4` |
| 5 | the third sector | the first crossings of the border (`x-4`) |
| 6 | the border (`x-4`) | – |
| 7 | the border | runs into the PvP centre (`DS-x`) |
| 8 | the border | the centre, and other companies' borders |

- **Patrols count outside safe zones only.** Circling a gate's ring doesn't patrol a sector.
- **A kill counts for one level mission**: the one you track, if it can use it, else the first of your active missions that can. Besides that it counts for every Challenge mission that asks for it, and every quest item step of yours that waits for that alien rolls its drop.
- An alien a [Company Pilot](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Company-Pilots.md) of yours finishes while you're fighting it counts as your kill, for your missions too.
- A kill by someone in your [group](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Groups.md) counts for your level missions too when you are on the same map and fired a laser or rocket at anything in the last 15 seconds. For the Challenge line the mate must also be within 4,000 units of the kill.

## Time limits

- Some missions are **timed**. Mission Control shows the limit on the mission's card before you accept it (a clock and "15 min"), and once you accept it a **countdown** runs on the card and in Active Quests. It turns amber in the last minute and red when time is up.
- A timed mission that runs out **fails**: it leaves your active missions and you can accept it again at once, from the start.
- The limits in the tables below are **Alpha's**. Beta's aliens are 1.5 times as strong and Gamma's twice, so their limits are 1.5 and 2 times as long. The clock is set when you accept the mission, for the world you're in.
- Steps have no time limit of their own: the mission's limit covers all of them. A broken condition restarts a step or the mission, but it never resets the clock.

## Rewards

- Experience, credits, Thulium and honor are multiplied by the [world](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Wipe-Timeline.md#worlds-alpha-beta-and-gamma) the mission was done in: 1x in Alpha, 2x in Beta, 3x in Gamma. Your boosters (the Experience Kit, the Honor Beacon) add to them, and premium doubles the experience. The Thulium and credits boosts of your [clan](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Clans.md) add to the credits and the Thulium of every mission you claim: level, Station and Challenge.
- **Station and Challenge missions pay like level missions.** The numbers printed in their tables are the **base**. A Challenge mission is paid by the world you did it in, like a level mission (the lowest one, should it span two). A Station mission has no world of its own: it pays the world you fly in when you claim it.
- **An example.** **Seeker Plague** (Challenge) has a base of 1,100,000 credits, 8,260 Thulium, 31,500 XP and 3,060 honor. Done and claimed in Gamma with nothing switched on, it pays 3,300,000 credits, 24,780 Thulium, 94,500 XP and 9,180 honor. With your clan's Credits and Thulium boosts at their top (+10% each) it pays 3,630,000 credits and 27,258 Thulium.
- **The clan bank cap.** However big a claim is, a pilot can send at most 1,000,000 credits into [clans](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Clans.md#2-donations) in any 24 hours.
- **Items and booster time are the same in every world.** Items go to your inventory, booster hours add to what the booster has left, and ammo is ready to fire even if you claim while flying.

## The reworked missions {#reworked-missions}

Update 0.4.10 reworked the level missions into chains. **64 of the 88 are new versions**; the 24 that stayed as they were are the plain kill missions (like Basic Training: Combat) and the Specials of levels 1, 2 and 5 to 8.

If you had **done** one of the 64, you do the new version too. At your first flight after the update a System line tells you: "Mission Control has new missions: the level quests were reworked."

- **The mission is offered again.** It is back in Mission Control, and it pays its **full reward** again: experience, credits, Thulium, honor and items, by the world you do it in.
- **A Special locks again** until the level's regular missions are done again, so level 3's ten missions come before Hive Breaker once more.
- **A reward you had not claimed yet** is paid as before (the larger of the old and the new reward), and then the new version is offered.
- **A mission you had running** is carried over to its new steps by the share you had done. A visit counts only when its share is whole, and a quest item is never handed in by that conversion.
- **Nothing goes down.** Your level, your statistics and your Wipe Points stay. A mission you do again does not count for the [Wipe Points](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Wipe-Timeline.md#earning-wipe-points) a second time: it was counted the first time.
- The Station missions, the Challenge line and the 24 missions that stayed are not touched.

## Danger

The higher sectors are where the missions pay, and where you can die. Plan your kit for them:

- **PvP**: other companies' pilots can attack you in `x-4` and the centre in every world, from `x-2` up in Beta, and everywhere in Gamma (except in safe zones and during the Peace Protocol). The ring gates bring other companies' pilots into your `x-3` too: in Beta and Gamma one of them can destroy you there while you carry an item.
- **Bulwarks** (`x-3`, `x-4`) outrun a Protos and hit hard. Fight them from an [Ostirion](/wiki/02-Ships/Ostirion.md), near a gate's safe zone, and pull back into it to repair.
- **Goombahs** (`x-3`, `x-4`) have a range of 800, hit for 3,000 and never start a fight: leave one alone and it leaves you alone, shoot it and it turns on you until 10 seconds after your last hit (and it mends when left alone). A ship whose lasers are all [Starfire-3](/wiki/06-Items/Lasers.md) (range 850) outranges them and Bulwarks alike: with a ship faster than they are (an Ostirion or above; a Goombah flies 180, a Bulwark 175) you can fire without taking a hit. Your ship's range is the average of its lasers' ranges, so a Starfire-3 beside two Quantum Laser 2 fires from 750: far enough to keep away from a Bulwark (700), not from a Goombah (800). Level 5's Special gives you one; you can also make one in Assembly, from Velkonite Reinforced Plates that the Forgery of your [Skylab](/wiki/03-Mechanics/Skylab.md) makes.
- **Crystalys** roam the border (`x-4`). Nothing in reach of level 8 outranges one, and only a fast ship outruns it: keep your distance, and watch the minimap.
- When you are destroyed you choose where to come back: at your base, at the nearest portal or on the spot (see [Dying and Coming Back](/wiki/01-General/Getting-Started.md)). A timed mission's clock keeps running meanwhile, a carried item is lost, and a no-death rule breaks.

## The missions

The time limits are Alpha's ("–": none). "→" joins the steps of an **In order** mission, which must be done in that order; steps joined by ";" open together and can be done in any order. A condition written after a step belongs to that step, "(whole mission: ...)" to every step.

A quest item reads "may drop it: 15% a kill, for certain at kill 10": every kill of that alien in that sector rolls the chance, and the 10th kill since the step opened drops it for sure. "From season day 4" is a [swarm hunt](#swarm-missions).
